report.summary: All 26 tests error during session setup because the app process exits with code 1 before it answers /health. The cause is a missing comma in the books table DDL in app/main.py (line 38), which makes the schema script fail on import. Fix that line first; the tests should then run again without other changes.

causes.title: Missing comma in books table DDL stops the app from starting
causes.explanation: The SCHEMA string in app/main.py defines the books table with no comma after the owner_id column. SQLite reads 'owner_id INTEGER NOT NULL title TEXT NOT NULL,' as one malformed column definition. The schema runs at import time (app/main.py:57-58: 'with db() as _conn: _conn.executescript(SCHEMA)'), so importing app.main raises and uvicorn exits with code 1. The conftest fixture base_url (tests/conftest.py:55-65) then sees proc.poll() return 1 and raises 'App exited early with code 1'. This fails on every run, so it is a real product bug, not flakiness. Every test that uses the base_url fixture (directly or through api, user, new_user, anon_api, other_api, or the UI fixtures) errors at setup, which is why all 26 tests are in this group.
evidence:
app/main.py:36-39: "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS books (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    owner_id INTEGER NOT NULL
    title TEXT NOT NULL," (no comma after 'owner_id INTEGER NOT NULL')
app/main.py:57-58: "with db() as _conn:\n    _conn.executescript(SCHEMA)" runs at import time
tests/conftest.py:34-35: "if proc.poll() is not None:\n    raise RuntimeError(f\"App exited early with code {proc.returncode}\")"

get_failure tests.api.test_auth_api::test_login_returns_token: 'RuntimeError: App exited early with code 1' raised from tests\conftest.py:35 in _wait_until_up, with proc returncode 1 for 'python -m uvicorn app.main:app'
Not directly seen: the uvicorn stderr traceback. The app was not run, so the SQLite syntax error is inferred from reading the DDL, not from captured output.
causes.suggested_fix: In app/main.py, add the missing comma after 'owner_id INTEGER NOT NULL' in the books CREATE TABLE statement so it reads 'owner_id INTEGER NOT NULL,'. Then run 'python -m uvicorn app.main:app' locally, or import app.main, to confirm it starts. Consider moving the schema creation out of import time, or at least logging the error, so a broken schema is easier to see. No test changes are needed.
